items.headline: Jensen Huang admits affair in Sunday statement as Nvidia installs Kress, names first-ever board chair
items.summary: On Sunday Nov 15, Huang issued a statement admitting to the affair underlying his Nov 12 forced resignation and apologized to his family and Nvidia employees; reports allege a separate affair with a suspected Chinese-intelligence-linked individual. CFO Colette Kress remains interim CEO while the board, now chaired for the first time by Harvey C. Jones, searches for a permanent successor.
items.actionable: The espionage allegation plus a confirmed leadership vacuum extends the AI-confidence crisis dragging semis/AI sentiment into Monday -- watch SMIC (0981.HK) and the HSTech complex for a continued weak open rather than a dead-cat bounce.

items.headline: Crypto weekend rout deepens: BTC near $63-65k, ETH below $1,850, $14.2B stablecoin drain
items.summary: Bitcoin extended its slide through the weekend, down roughly 14% over seven days toward $63,400-65,400 depending on venue, with $1.6B+ in 24h liquidations (mostly longs) on Nov 12 alone. Ethereum fell to ~$1,824-1,875, its weakest since July, on six straight days of spot-ETF outflows and forced liquidations; aggregate stablecoin market cap contracted ~$14.2B over 7 days to $284.8B. Analysts tie the cascade to macro deleveraging (Fed hike fears, ~5.15% Treasury yields) compounding the Nvidia/Huang shock.
items.actionable: Confirms a genuine weekend risk-off/deleveraging mood heading into Monday's Asia open -- expect carryover pressure on HK tech, and no 'flight to metals' bid this cycle since silver/gold are also trading as risk assets right now.

items.headline: December Fed hike odds near 90%; Waller floats a 50bp move
items.summary: After Friday's hot PPI (wholesale prices +6.5% y/y, a 4-year high) confirmed Tuesday's hot CPI, CME FedWatch pushed December hike odds to ~88.5% for 25bp (and ~11.5% for 50bp). Fed Governor Waller said a 50bp hike 'should be considered' given core CPI printed 0.3% for a third straight month, raising the stakes for the Oct PCE report (Nov 25).
items.actionable: Rate-repricing risk (possibly 50bp, not just 25bp) is the dominant near-term headwind for the silver/miner sleeve into the Dec 8-9 FOMC -- avoid adding on weakness until that uncertainty clears.

items.headline: Taiwan detects fresh PLA activity Saturday as China's 'silent intimidation' drills continue
items.summary: Taiwan's Ministry of National Defense reported detecting 10 PLA aircraft, 8 warships and 3 China coast guard vessels around the island on Saturday Nov 14, following an earlier unannounced large-scale PLA exercise involving 100+ vessels across multiple theater commands and the Liaoning carrier group -- described by Taipei as deliberate pressure timed before major international meetings.
items.actionable: A rising, still-contained Taiwan Strait tail-risk overhang for the HK tech sleeve into Monday's open -- no action warranted yet, but it compounds (not replaces) the Nvidia-driven HSTech weakness.

items.headline: Hang Seng tumbles 1.55% to 23,637.60, HSTech -3%, Alibaba -7% on Nvidia-scandal fallout
items.summary: Friday's HK close saw the Hang Seng Index fall 370.95 points (1.55%) and the Hang Seng Tech Index drop 3.02%, extending a three-session losing streak. Alibaba fell 7% (its worst day since August) and Hua Hong Semiconductor fell 6.1% as investors priced in fallout from the Nvidia CEO scandal, while PetroChina (+2.79%) bucked the trend on firmer oil.
items.actionable: Direct read-through for Tencent (0700.HK) and the HSTech complex going into Monday's open -- the weekend's further BTC/ETH deleveraging raises the odds of another weak Asia tech open rather than stabilization.

items.headline: Silver deficit forecast widens to 46.3Moz but price fell 3.6% Friday on rate pressure
items.summary: Metals Focus/Silver Institute now project a 46.3M-oz 2026 global silver deficit (vs 40.3Moz in 2025) -- a sixth straight annual shortfall -- but COMEX flows are ambiguous: eligible stocks fell ~6Moz since Oct 27 while registered stocks rose ~4Moz (metal reshuffling, not necessarily tightening). Silver still closed Friday down ~2.2-3.6% depending on the quote venue to roughly $44-51/oz as the stronger dollar/rate-hike repricing overwhelmed the deficit narrative.
items.actionable: The structural squeeze thesis is intact long-term, but Friday's drop was rate-driven, not supply-driven -- don't read the pullback as a thesis break for the silver/miner core position; a mid-November interim deficit review is due and worth watching.

items.headline: China extends rare-earth export-control suspension to January 10, 2027; dysprosium/terbium/yttrium curbs stay in force
items.summary: China's Ministry of Commerce extended by two months (to Jan 10, 2027) the pause on the broad rare-earth/battery export controls that had been due to lapse in November, part of the wider trade-truce framework with Washington ahead of the Nov 18-19 APEC summit in Shenzhen. Licensing requirements on dysprosium, terbium and yttrium were explicitly left intact, and dysprosium oxide prices outside China have reportedly surged ~242% to around $4,100/kg this year despite the broader pause.
items.actionable: Removes the near-term tail risk of a sudden re-imposition of the widest export controls, but heavy rare-earth curbs (dysprosium/terbium/yttrium) staying intact keeps a structural price floor under MP/Lynas magnet-supply-chain names -- the Jan 10, 2027 date and the Nov 18-19 Trump-Xi Shenzhen meeting are the next catalysts to watch.

items.headline: MP Materials clears GM magnet-qualification milestone; three insiders buy $3.35M on Form 4
items.summary: MP Materials completed General Motors magnet qualification, a concrete step toward becoming a vertically integrated US magnet supplier, and is reportedly targeting Apple as a next customer, on the back of a Q3 revenue beat (+176% y/y to $147.7M). A director, the COO and the CFO bought a combined ~$3.35M of stock on Nov 10-11, verified directly against SEC Form 4 XML filings.
items.actionable: A tangible commercial proof point plus a genuine three-insider buying cluster strengthens the ex-China magnet thesis underpinning the MP position on the rare-earth watchlist.

items.headline: Houthis strike Saudi East-West pipeline, Yanbu oil facility, and an Aramco building in Riyadh
items.summary: Yemen's Houthis claimed drone/missile strikes on Thursday Nov 12 against Pumping Station No. 7 of the Saudi East-West crude pipeline, a Yanbu oil facility, and an Aramco building in Riyadh; the Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted two of the drones. Brent held near $96/bbl into the weekend on this plus stalled US-Iran talks, with oil futures trading suspended Nov 14-15 over the weekend.
items.actionable: No direct portfolio holding, but sustained Red Sea/Saudi energy-infrastructure risk is part of the geopolitical-risk-premium backdrop propping up gold/silver even as rate fears bite -- context for the precious-metals sleeve, not a standalone trade.

items.headline: Commerce Secretary Lutnick agrees to testify over Nvidia chip-export oversight tied to Singapore-based Megaspeed
items.summary: Lutnick agreed to testify before the Senate Banking Committee (hearings set for Dec 3 and Dec 10, alongside ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang) after it emerged the Commerce Department knew for two years about a Bureau of Industry and Security probe into Megaspeed -- a Singapore-based buyer of over $4.8B of Nvidia's high-end AI chips -- without placing it on the export-restricted list; the probe, now with the DOJ, concerns whether those chips were diverted to China.
items.actionable: A Singapore-incorporated entity now sits at the center of the US chip-export enforcement failure story, adding idiosyncratic headline risk around the Singapore-exposure complex and keeping the chip-export-control overhang on Chinese tech alive through the Dec 3/10 hearings.

items.headline: Singapore bank Q3 split confirmed: OCBC beats and raises guidance; DBS and UOB miss
items.summary: OCBC's Q3 net profit rose 3% y/y to S$2.04B, beating estimates, and management raised 2026 loan-growth guidance; DBS's net profit fell ~5% y/y, missing consensus, with both DBS and UOB weighed down by weaker trading income. Asset quality improved across all three (NPLs 0.8-0.9%).
items.actionable: OCBC's guidance raise supports the relative-strength case for that name within the SGX bank sleeve, while DBS's miss and trading-income weakness -- now compounding with the hawkish Fed repricing -- argues for keeping DBS exposure smaller than OCBC into year-end.

items.headline: Keppel REIT to acquire 51% of Keppel South Central; 9M 2026 net property income up 12.7%
items.summary: Keppel REIT announced at its Nov 12 Investor Day a proposed acquisition of a 51% interest in Keppel South Central, a newly completed 33-storey Grade-A office tower in Tanjong Pagar. For the nine months ended Sep 30, 2026, the REIT reported net property income of S$181.8M, up 12.7% year-on-year.
items.actionable: An accretive, income-generating acquisition plus double-digit NPI growth is a fundamental positive for the Keppel REIT leg of the SGX book, offsetting some of the discount-rate pressure from the hawkish Fed repricing.

items.headline: Keppel's Rigco and Seatrium ink S$500M+ offshore rig contract
items.summary: Keppel's wholly owned subsidiary Rigco and Seatrium will jointly complete four offshore rigs under a contract worth more than S$500 million, with a drillship due in 2027 and a jackup rig in 2028. Seatrium separately secured a contract to convert five hydrogen-ready Powerships.
items.actionable: Direct positive order-book news reinforcing offshore/marine demand within the SGX industrial sleeve (Seatrium).
